chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Give them the writing if you know any good in them, and give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You reduce from his installments (the agreed portions) which you did not intend to deduct from them, and do not exceed what is in your mind (or what you agreed upon).' So I said, 'How much?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) reduced from his owned slave one thousand from six thousand.'

key_terms.فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ: give them the writing (contract of manumission)
key_terms.نُجُومِهِ: his installments (plural of najm, referring to scheduled payments)

ai.seo_question: How much can a master reduce from a slave's contract price during kitabah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the principle of 'Ikram' (generosity) in kitabah contracts, distinguishing between the legal obligation to accept payment and the spiritual merit of voluntarily forgiving portions of the debt. It highlights the Shia emphasis on benevolence in manumission, where the master's intention determines the extent of forgiveness, as exemplified by the Imam’s reduction of his slave’s debt from six thousand to five thousand dinars. This legal nuance encourages masters to view manumission not merely as a transaction but as an act of divine grace.
